microtheory.name: economics
microtheory.definition: Economics — production, distribution, consumption of goods + services; allocation of scarce resources. Smith, Ricardo, Marx, Marshall, Keynes, Hayek, Friedman, Samuelson, Krugman, Piketty. Micro (individual agents, markets) + macro (aggregates, growth, business cycles). Substrate analogue: the discipline of resource allocation under scarcity + the behaviour of populations of self-interested agents.

concepts.name: scarcity_economic
concepts.definition: Resources are limited; wants are unlimited. Foundational fact requiring economic choice. Substrate analogue: substrate's bounded-resource allocation.

concepts.name: opportunity_cost
concepts.definition: Value of next-best foregone alternative. Every choice has one. Substrate analogue: substrate's drive-tradeoff cost.

concepts.name: supply_demand
concepts.definition: Marshall 1890. Market price + quantity determined by supply (sellers) + demand (buyers) intersection. Substrate analogue: substrate's equilibrium-finding mechanism.

concepts.name: equilibrium_market
concepts.definition: Price where quantity supplied = quantity demanded. Self-adjusting via price signals.

concepts.name: marginal_analysis
concepts.definition: Decisions made at margin. Marginal cost vs marginal benefit. Diminishing marginal utility (Gossen, Jevons).

concepts.name: smith_invisible_hand
concepts.definition: Adam Smith 1776. Individuals pursuing self-interest unintentionally promote social good through market coordination. Wealth of Nations.

concepts.name: ricardo_comparative_advantage
concepts.definition: David Ricardo 1817. Trade benefits both parties when each specialises in relatively-lower-cost production.

concepts.name: marx_capital
concepts.definition: Karl Marx. Surplus value extracted from labor. Crisis tendencies of capitalism. Class struggle as engine of history.

concepts.name: marshall_neoclassical
concepts.definition: Alfred Marshall. Mathematical formalisation of supply-demand. Marginalist revolution synthesis.

concepts.name: keynes_general_theory
concepts.definition: John Maynard Keynes 1936. Aggregate demand drives economy; recessions from insufficient demand; government fiscal policy can stabilise.

concepts.name: hayek_knowledge_problem
concepts.definition: Friedrich Hayek. Prices aggregate dispersed knowledge no central planner could possess. Foundation of market-information argument.

concepts.name: friedman_monetarism
concepts.definition: Milton Friedman. Money supply primary driver of price level. Permanent income hypothesis. Critique of Keynesian fine-tuning.

concepts.name: rational_choice
concepts.definition: Agents maximise utility subject to constraints. Foundational assumption of neoclassical. Behavioral economics relaxes.

concepts.name: utility_function
concepts.definition: Numerical representation of preferences. Ordinal (rank only) vs cardinal (magnitude). Substrate analogue: substrate's value function.

concepts.name: consumer_surplus
concepts.definition: Difference between willingness to pay + price paid. Welfare measure.

concepts.name: elasticity
concepts.definition: Responsiveness of one variable to another. Price elasticity of demand: %ΔQ / %ΔP.

concepts.name: perfect_competition
concepts.definition: Many small firms, homogeneous product, no entry barriers, full information. Price-taking. Idealised benchmark.

concepts.name: monopoly
concepts.definition: Single seller. Inefficient pricing above marginal cost. Substrate analogue: substrate's single-point-of-failure pattern.

concepts.name: oligopoly
concepts.definition: Few firms. Strategic interaction. Game theory required (Cournot, Bertrand, Stackelberg).

concepts.name: externality
concepts.definition: Cost or benefit imposed on third parties. Pollution (negative), vaccination (positive). Pigou taxes correct.

concepts.name: public_good
concepts.definition: Non-excludable + non-rivalrous. Defense, clean air. Free-rider problem → underprovision by market.

concepts.name: gdp
concepts.definition: Gross Domestic Product. Total value of final goods + services produced in territory + time. Standard output measure. Substrate analogue: substrate's aggregate-activity measure.

concepts.name: inflation
concepts.definition: General rise in price level. CPI, PCE indices. Hyperinflation destroys savings.

concepts.name: unemployment
concepts.definition: Working-age people seeking work but without job. Frictional, structural, cyclical types.

concepts.name: business_cycle
concepts.definition: Recurrent fluctuations in economic activity. Expansion → peak → contraction → trough. NBER dates US.

concepts.name: fiscal_policy
concepts.definition: Government spending + taxation. Counter-cyclical (Keynes) or balanced-budget. Multiplier effects.

concepts.name: monetary_policy
concepts.definition: Central bank control of money supply + interest rates. Inflation targeting, dual mandate. Federal Reserve, ECB.

concepts.name: phillips_curve
concepts.definition: Inverse short-run relation between unemployment + inflation. Friedman-Phelps natural rate critique.

concepts.name: behavioral_economics
concepts.definition: Kahneman + Tversky. Real agents deviate systematically from rational choice. Prospect theory, loss aversion, framing effects.

concepts.name: game_theory_econ
concepts.definition: Strategic interaction analysis. Nash equilibrium, Pareto optimality, repeated games. Foundation of industrial organisation.

concepts.name: information_asymmetry
concepts.definition: Akerlof, Spence, Stiglitz. Adverse selection, moral hazard, signalling. Markets fail under asymmetric information.

concepts.name: principal_agent
concepts.definition: Principal hires agent to act on behalf. Agent's interests may diverge. Mechanism design corrects.

concepts.name: transaction_cost
concepts.definition: Coase 1937. Costs of market transactions explain why firms exist. Williamson extends to governance.

concepts.name: endogenous_growth
concepts.definition: Romer. Long-run growth driven by ideas (non-rival) + human capital. Investment in R&D + education yields persistent growth.

rules.name: scarcity_forces_tradeoffs
rules.head: Jabberwock allocates resources
rules.body: every choice has opportunity cost — the value of next-best foregone alternative. No free lunch. Substrate's drive-balancing principle.

rules.name: supply_meets_demand_at_price
rules.head: Jabberwock models a market
rules.body: supply + demand intersect at equilibrium price; quantity supplied = quantity demanded. Self-adjusting via price signals (Marshall 1890).

rules.name: comparative_advantage_justifies_trade
rules.head: Jabberwock considers specialisation
rules.body: even when one party is absolutely better at everything, both gain from specialisation in their comparative advantage (Ricardo 1817).

rules.name: externalities_distort_prices
rules.head: Jabberwock observes systematic misallocation
rules.body: external costs/benefits not borne by transacting parties lead to over/underproduction. Pigou taxes correct. Substrate's third-party-effect mechanism.

rules.name: loss_aversion_violates_rational_choice
rules.head: Jabberwock observes real decision-making
rules.body: Kahneman + Tversky: losses loom ~2× larger than equivalent gains. People deviate systematically from rational-choice model. Substrate's behavioral correction.
